862b73.risk_area: Infrastructure security: SG exposure, IAM wildcards, S3 public access, TLS, VPC placement
862b73.evidence: SG ingress limited to 80/443 via AllowedCidr param (default 0.0.0.0/0 — noted as combined risk factor in vuln-0005); DB/Redis SGs allow only from EC2 SG; RDS storage encrypted, not public, SecretsManager-generated creds; all 4 S3 buckets BLOCK_ALL public access + encryption; EBS encrypted. Weaknesses (wildcard bedrock-agentcore actions `resources:['*']`, `bedrock:InvokeModel` on `*`) are least-privilege hygiene for an AI app that legitimately invokes any model/runtime, not exploitable misconfigurations — observation only.

2df3ac.risk_area: Container security: root user, privileged, exposed ports, embedded credentials
2df3ac.evidence: Multi-stage build, USER node (non-root), no privileged, no embedded secrets (only non-secret ENV: model name, region, CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK flag), EXPOSE 8080 as required by AgentCore protocol. HOME set to /workspace by design. No issues.

5203a5.risk_area: Container/process security: root execution, embedded secrets
5203a5.evidence: Backend Dockerfile: multi-stage, non-root USER backend, no secrets baked in. systemd service runs as ubuntu user, .env chmod 600, JWT_SECRET generated at deploy time via openssl rand (deploy.sh:239) — good. Hardcoded local Redis password `super-agent-redis-password` in user-data.sh is a hygiene issue (localhost-bound fallback, ElastiCache path has no password set on the cluster — noted as observation, low impact since Redis SG is EC2-only and there is a redis AUTH gap only if SG were bypassed).

1cd352.surface: super-agent/frontend (build config, dangerouslySetInnerHTML, env files, hardcoded keys)
1cd352.risk_area: XSS via dangerouslySetInnerHTML, secret exposure, committed .env
1cd352.evidence: Only one dangerouslySetInnerHTML (Chat.tsx:470) and it renders hljs.highlight output — highlight.js HTML-escapes input before highlighting, standard safe pattern; catch branch also escapes manually. .env.example contains only placeholders; no committed secrets; .gitignore covers .env files (backend/.env exists locally but is git-ignored, dev-only values). No hardcoded API keys.

dc7d34.evidence: gitleaks repo scan: 1 hit only — generic-api-key in an industry-pack SKILL.md, which is a sample JSON token format in documentation (VT-MFA-...uuid), not a real credential — false positive. Backend .env committed? No — git-ignored, contains only dev values (sa:sa local). JWT_SECRET generated randomly at deploy (deploy.sh:239). Real finding: hardcoded default admin credential Admin1234! in deploy scripts + public docs — filed as vuln-0005. Observation: hardcoded local Redis password super-agent-redis-password in user-data.sh; ElastiCache cluster created with no auth token (stack line ~150) — mitigated by Redis SG restricting ingress to EC2 SG only.

b6f269.risk_area: Deployment config: exposed dashboards, docker.sock, default creds
b6f269.evidence: app-hosting/ contains only design docs (MD files) and a PoC docker-compose for a local simulator (floci = localstack-like, test AWS keys `test/test`, traefik insecure dashboard, postgres `apphost:apphost123`). It is an explicit local PoC not shipped in the production CDK stack; per instructions config hygiene in non-production dev tooling is an observation, not a vulnerability.

ef4297.risk_area: Insecure quick-start defaults that ship to production
ef4297.evidence: Default admin credential documented publicly (part of vuln-0005). Other observations: self-signed TLS cert on 443 in user-data.sh (users trained to click through warnings, no HSTS); CloudFront /api origin uses HTTP_ONLY to EC2 port 80; AllowedCidr default 0.0.0.0/0; Cognito callback URL localhost:5173 fixed in stack. All hygiene-level except the admin credential which is filed.

4ba917.surface: super-agent backend config defaults (config/index.ts JWT_SECRET, CORS, InsForge JWT)
4ba917.risk_area: Insecure default secrets enabling token forgery
4ba917.evidence: Superseded by filed finding vuln-0002 (hardcoded default JWT_SECRET, PoC-verified token forgery).

history.evidence: config/index.ts:30 defaults JWT_SECRET to 'super-agent-local-dev-secret-change-in-production' when unset. Deploy script always sets JWT_SECRET (deploy.sh:239), so production deployments via the provided path are safe; but any manual/Docker deployment that omits JWT_SECRET runs with a publicly-known signing secret → auth bypass. Whether such a deployment exists in production is unverifiable offline; the auth-team agent may already cover this (it was in the threat model). Flag for cross-check to avoid duplicate filing.

0b06f2.evidence: INTERNAL_TOKEN_SECRET = Cognito userPoolId (public) in cognito mode, default JWT secret in local mode; forged token accepted by offline PoC replicating auth.ts:115-129. Filed as vuln-0001 (critical). Also non-constant-time !== compare at auth.ts:121 noted in report.

594f33.surface: src/config/index.ts:30 + src/middleware/auth.ts:49-74 — local JWT secret handling
594f33.risk_area: Hardcoded default JWT secret / token forgery
594f33.evidence: Default 'super-agent-local-dev-secret-change-in-production' with no production guard anywhere in startup path; offline PoC (repo's jsonwebtoken) forged+verified owner-role token. Bootstrap user-data.sh writes CHANGE_ME placeholder. Filed as vuln-0002 (critical). INSFORGE_JWT_SECRET has same pattern (config/index.ts:145), noted in remediation.

119ad4.risk_area: Brute force / default credentials / password policy
119ad4.evidence: No rate limiting, lockout, or password policy on login/register; seed-local-auth.ts plants admin@example.com/admin123 owner account. Filed as vuln-0003 (critical).

1580bc.evidence: Query token accepted app-wide; requestLogger.ts:57 logs full URL with token; app.ts:54 redact list omits query string. Filed as vuln-0004 (low).

40c141.surface: src/services/apiKey.service.ts — API key generation and validation
40c141.evidence: Keys are 32 random bytes with sk_ prefix, stored as SHA-256 hash, lookup by unique index on hash (no enumeration oracle — uniform 401), expiry and revocation enforced, rate limit per key via Redis. Hash lookup is not a timing-compare of secrets (hash is not secret material in the timing-attack sense; 256-bit preimage). No weakness found.

56ee6f.evidence: Widget issues no tokens of its own: it authenticates existing api_keys by SHA-256 hash, requires widget:connect scope and active+unexpired key, scopes all queries to the key's organization (org-scoped findFirst on sessions/messages). Runs as WIDGET_SYSTEM_USER_ID. No over-issuance or unauthenticated widget route found. Note: uses raw sha256 lookup like apiKeyService (consistent) — fine.

3a6e2a.surface: src/app.ts CORS registration + config/index.ts:64 CORS_ORIGIN default
3a6e2a.evidence: origin:true (reflects any origin) + credentials:true, default '*'. No cookie auth exists, so impact currently limited — filed as vuln-0007 (medium).

02a8c0.surface: src/middleware/auth.ts:190-255 — verifyToken claims handling + Cognito email binding
02a8c0.risk_area: Claim trust / account takeover via email binding
02a8c0.evidence: Email-based first-login binding reassigns all profile rows without checking email_verified (verifier config auth.ts:17-21 doesn't enforce it); custom:role/custom:orgId trusted as fallbacks. Conditional on pool configuration — filed as vuln-0006 (medium, confidence medium).

d55fdc.evidence: Raw bearer token compared against key_hash column which stores sha256(key) — all valid keys rejected; reliability defect, no security impact. Filed as vuln-0008 (info).

6e06b6.surface: src/routes/* — unauthenticated route inventory (health, im webhooks, widget, openapi, a2a, app backends)
6e06b6.evidence: Swept all 50 route files: health (intended public), auth (login/register/invite by design, invite tokens validated + expiry enforced), im webhook routes verify per-adapter signatures (other agent's scope), widget routes require api key with widget:connect, openapi routes use apiKeyAuth (correct sha256 path), a2a requires API key (broken but rejects everything). No missing-auth route found.

a2efab.evidence: fetch sites take an `endpoint` param, but all current callers construct endpoints as `local://${agentId}` only (chatRooms.routes.ts:292 is the sole producer of AgentEndpoint lists, plus orchestrator passing them through). No user-supplied remote https:// endpoint exists in any route or DB field today; remote path is dead code for attacker input. Would become SSRF if external agent endpoints are added.

b3763c.evidence: llm-proxy proxies to Bedrock only (BedrockRuntimeClient), no user-controllable upstream URL; litellm.routes.ts fetches config.litellm.baseUrl (server-side env), not user input. No arbitrary-upstream proxy primitive found.

0f0b80.risk_area: Missing/forged signature verification on state-changing callbacks
0f0b80.evidence: Confirmed end-to-end: adapters (slack:39, telegram:31, dingtalk:80, whatsapp:66, feishu:104) return true when no secret configured; discord:23 and wecom:177 always return true. Route chain verifyAndLookupBinding (im.routes.ts:226-271) does global binding lookup (no org) then adapter.verifyRequest → imService.handleMessage → chatService.processMessage with binding org/scope/created_by. Executed the project's own adapters in isolated sandbox: verifyRequest({}, body) → true for all four; control with secret + forged signature → false. Generic POST /api/im/webhook/:bindingId has no verification at all. Filed as vuln-0026. Prerequisites: at least one enabled binding without a stored secret (or Discord/WeCom binding, or known generic-webhook binding UUID).

history.evidence: Slack: timing-safe HMAC verify (good) but URL-verification challenge answered before any signature check, and any binding without signing_secret configured passes verifyRequest trivially (returns true when secret header absent). DingTalk (hmac === sign, non-timing-safe), Feishu (token equality, non-timing-safe), WhatsApp/Telegram/DingTalk all `return true` when no secret configured; Discord and WeCom generic path verifyRequest always return true (Discord relies on gateway mode; its verifyRequest ignores the public_key injected in im.routes.ts). WeCom agent mode does verify SHA1 signature + AES decrypt properly. Default-open verification means forged messages can be injected when secrets are unset. Could not run a live PoC (needs DB/bindings), so left as open gap.

a3657e.evidence: api-spec-parser parses content only — no fetch of remote spec URLs; integrations route accepts specContent string. avatarRoutes uploads file buffers to S3 (sharp), no URL fetch. connectors.routes CRUD only (testConnection checks credential status, no network fetch). browser-live-view has no fetch of user URLs. No outbound URL sink in these files.

5fef49.evidence: Filed vuln-0012: client secrets encrypted with hardcoded default key + static salt; upsert accepts arbitrary provider names. OAuth flow itself: state is 32-byte random, in-memory, 10-min expiry, provider matched — adequate; redirect_uri is server-constructed; token URLs hardcoded to google/salesforce so no attacker-directed token exchange today.

38f087.surface: Workflow api_call action node (action-executor.ts, workflow-orchestrator.ts) + MCP server test (mcp.service.ts)
38f087.risk_area: SSRF / unrestricted outbound fetch of user-controlled URL
38f087.evidence: Filed vuln-0009 (api_call SSRF, includes unauthenticated webhook-variable chain) and vuln-0010 (MCP test endpoint SSRF). Both demonstrated with local vitest PoCs against local mock HTTP servers.

cbb335.surface: Webhook trigger + public status endpoints (webhooks.routes.ts, webhook.service.ts)
cbb335.risk_area: Unauthenticated state change / missing signature verification
cbb335.evidence: Filed vuln-0011: secret_hash generated but never verified anywhere in the codebase; trigger is unauthenticated by design with no HMAC; IP allowlist optional and skipped when unset; GET /v1/webhook/status/:callRecordId publicly exposes execution node detail.

98978c.evidence: readWorkspaceFile/writeWorkspaceFile/writeWorkspaceFileRaw/resolveWorkspaceFilePath all apply `resolved.startsWith(workspacePath)` after join (lines 1476, 1555, 1569, 1605); `..` segments are resolved by join and fail the prefix check. Sibling-prefix bypass (startsWith without trailing separator) is only exploitable if another org/scope/session ID is a strict string prefix of the victim's — all components are random UUIDs, so not practically reachable; recorded as a reliability note. Symlink-following during writes is inherent to the workspace model (the agent runtime owns the workspace).

8e469c.evidence: join(skillsDir, skillName) + cp with no containment check; skill name attacker-controlled via zip upload/installRef. Demonstrated arbitrary write outside workspace base with the real module (vuln-0013).

e99b98.evidence: runCommand wraps in /bin/bash -c with shellEscape that only escapes quotes/backslashes; skill names interpolated at skill-marketplace.routes.ts:158 and enterprise-skill.service.ts:338 without sanitizePath (vuln-0014, demonstrated locally). readFile/writeFile/deleteFile/deleteDirectory/syncFileFromS3 are guarded by sanitizePath which blocks .., /, and shell metacharacters — those wrappers are safe.

5f1e60.evidence: Upload sanitizes filename (replaces /\\:*?"<>| with '-'), storage_path built from server-generated randomUUID at group creation; delete uses DB-stored stored_filename scoped by org. RAG indexer joins storagePath+storedFilename from DB records under org-scoped group. No traversal vector found. DOC_GROUPS_BASE_PATH itself is not user-influenced.

558e31.risk_area: IDOR / key traversal in object storage
558e31.evidence: All key operations validate key.startsWith(`${orgId}/`) (file.service.ts validateFileAccess); filenames sanitized to [a-zA-Z0-9.-]. S3 keys are not filesystem paths, so traversal is limited to prefix escaping — blocked by the org-prefix check.

45522a.surface: Skill marketplace upload-zip / import / install (skill-marketplace.service.ts, routes)
45522a.risk_area: Archive extraction (zip-slip) and unsafe skill install
45522a.evidence: Confirmed by local PoC (vuln-0029): unix symlink members survive `unzip -o -q` (skill-marketplace.service.ts:800) and `fs.cp(..., {recursive:true})` without verbatimSymlinks (line 843; workspace-manager.ts:1361, :976) dereferences them — out-of-archive file content copied into attacker-readable skill storage. Classic `..` zip-slip is blocked by unzip/tar defaults; the symlink path is the exploitable variant.

history.evidence: Extraction uses system `unzip -o -q` (and tar fallback for .tar.gz) into a temp dir; Info-ZIP unzip and GNU tar both refuse `..` entries by default, so classic zip-slip appears blocked, but symlink members inside archives followed by Node fs.cp (verbatimSymlinks not set) were not dynamically tested — a zip containing a symlink to a sensitive dir could cause out-of-bounds copy during `cp(skillDir, permDir)`. Also `npx skills add` with repoRef in installRef (skill-marketplace.service.ts:402) runs an npm package fetch path worth an npx-confusion review (custom `npx_confusion` skill) not performed here. The skill-NAME traversal consequence of these endpoints is reported (vuln-0013/0014).

7d508f.evidence: All spawns use argv arrays with no shell: `spawn('npx', ['vite','--port',...])`, `npm install`, `git clone` via execFile with literal args — no interpolation of user data into argv. Ports are randomly selected and only the session that owns the workspace can trigger a server. Running npm install/npx vite over agent-generated package.json in the session's own workspace is intended agent functionality, not a guard failure. Plugin gitUrl/ref come from DB (operator-configured plugins), executed via execFile with array args — no injection.

800fba.evidence: packId and scopeDirName are joined into paths under the server-side industry-packs directory, but all reads are gated by `existsSync(packDir)` / `existsSync(resolvedDir)` and only directory reads (readdir of agents/skills subdirs) occur — a traversal name resolves to a non-existent directory and returns 404 before any file is parsed; no write or delete uses these inputs. Content read is limited to files inside the resolved dir via fixed names (scope.json, SKILL.md, workflow-plan.json). No containment escape is reachable because traversal requires an existing directory at the escaped path and everything is read-only.

d0a101.risk_area: Upload validation / unauthenticated access / content-type confusion
d0a101.evidence: Upload validates mimetype allowlist, re-encodes everything through sharp to 128x128 WebP (destroys any embedded payload), server-generated S3 key. GET /avatars/* has no authenticate preHandler (minor unauthenticated read of avatar objects, keys timestamp+random — low, noted) but content-type is forced to image/png|webp and the bucket is avatar-only; no stored-XSS or traversal (S3 keys, not FS paths). GET /avatars/presign/:key is authenticated; it can presign any key in the avatars bucket but that bucket holds only generated/re-encoded images.

a6d259.surface: Claude runtime subprocess + workflow node executors (agent-runtime-claude.ts, claude-agent.service.ts, claude-config.ts, claude-hooks.ts, node-executors/*)
a6d259.evidence: Claude runs via the official SDK with options object (pathToClaudeCodeExecutable from server config only, claude-agent.service.ts:421) — no shell string, no user data in argv. No exec/spawn/eval/new Function/vm found in node-executors/* (action/agent/document/code-artifact executors dispatch to LLM and API calls, not shell). claude-hooks.ts is a regex denylist for agent output content (prompt guardrail), not a command path.

466e15.surface: S3 workspace sync paths (skill-marketplace.routes.ts:197, enterprise-skill.service.ts:298, workspace-manager ensureS3SyncedToLocal)
466e15.risk_area: S3 key prefix escape via skill name
466e15.evidence: destKey built as `${s3Prefix}.claude/skills/${result.name}` with unsanitized skill name — `../` in the name escapes the per-session prefix, enabling cross-session/cross-object overwrite in the workspace bucket; folded into vuln-0013 impact. ensureS3SyncedToLocal derives local paths from S3 keys (server/container-written) — not directly attacker-controlled.

6432f5.evidence: All task CRUD passes orgId into taskService and BaseRepository enforces organization_id predicates on findById/update/delete (base.repository.ts:163-260). Routes all apply authenticate (+ requireModifyAccess on writes).

6e4cc1.evidence: Every /sessions/:id handler calls chatService.getSessionById(id, request.user.orgId) before touching workspace/files; BaseRepository enforces org predicate. Star endpoints also scoped. (Note: session sharing within org is by design; user_id not checked but org-scoped — horizontal access inside one org is the documented model.)

1119f4.evidence: Leader endpoint (chatRooms.routes.ts:177-206) confirmed NOT protected: raw prisma.chat_room_members.updateMany filters only on session_id/agent_id with no organization_id predicate and no room-ownership lookup on this route (preHandlers are authenticate + role-only requireModifyAccess). Filed as vuln-0025. Other room handlers on the file do scope via orgId (e.g. removeMember line 159).

history.evidence: Room lifecycle, members, messages all resolve via chatSessionRepository.findById(roomId, orgId) or service methods that verify room belongs to org first. Leader endpoint (chatRooms.routes.ts:177-206) uses raw prisma updateMany on chat_room_members by session_id without org predicate, but the route has requireModifyAccess and the effect is limited to leader flag within attacker's org — verified reachability requires cross-org session id which fails FK/room checks upstream only informally; see open item.

230010.evidence: All id-based agent routes apply authenticate + requireAgentAccess(view/admin/owner); agentAccessService.checkAccess enforces org via prisma.agents.findFirst({id, organization_id}) (agentAccess.service.ts:62-67). agentPermissions.routes not in depth but middleware itself is sound. Mass assignment: updateAgentSchema has no organization_id/created_by fields (agent.schema.ts:48-73).

0dd37b.risk_area: Member-configurable stdio MCP server command execution / tool dispatch trust
0dd37b.evidence: Any org member (requireModifyAccess includes 'member') can create an MCP server with arbitrary stdio command/args/env (POST /api/mcp/servers); config flows unvalidated through parseMCPServerConfig into the Claude SDK spawn config and workspace settings.json; PoC script in /tmp/tdpoc/mcp-config-poc.mts shows node -e payload passes through verbatim.

6f92f2.evidence: getDocumentById/updateDocument/deleteDocument all call documentRepository.findById(id, organizationId); BaseRepository org-scoped. Update schema lacks organization_id binding (no mass assignment).

f92870.risk_area: Prompt-injection-to-sensitive-action: bypassable Bash denylist under permissionMode bypassPermissions
f92870.evidence: PoC (/tmp/tdpoc/hooks-bypass.poc.mts) shows curl exfiltration, base64|sh, sh -c $(curl), variable-indirected rm -rf, node -e code exec all pass the hook; buildOptions sets permissionMode 'bypassPermissions', allowDangerouslySkipPermissions, allowedTools Bash/Write/Edit/WebFetch.

8bd0dc.evidence: credentialVaultRepository.findById and dataConnectorService methods all take orgId and use findFirst with organization_id. Credential read strips encrypted material. OAuth callback unauthenticated but state-validated (out of my scope).

166d4b.risk_area: Cross-tenant BOLA on checkpoint resolve/resume and execution read
166d4b.evidence: resolve() uses findUnique by checkpoint id with no organization filter; GET /api/workflows/executions/:executionId (checkpoint.routes) uses findUnique without org_id; workflowExecutorV2.resume loads execution by findUnique without org filter and route passes user-supplied scopeId. All routes preHandler authenticate only.

4783b8.risk_area: IDOR / vertical access control / mass assignment
4783b8.evidence: updateMembership/removeMember require owner|admin and membershipRepository.findById(id, orgId) is org-scoped; owner-role promotion is blocked (organization.service.ts:358-365). Provision endpoint restricted to owner|admin and binds to caller org. No body-bindable orgId/role escalation found (role changes validated against enum and admin gate).

6d91a6.surface: mcp.routes.ts + skills.routes.ts + projects.routes.ts + workshop.routes.ts + document-groups.routes.ts (main group CRUD)
6d91a6.evidence: MCP, skills, projects, workshop and document-group primary CRUD all funnel orgId through BaseRepository or explicit organization_id predicates (verified service/repository calls). appData/appBackend also org-scoped on every query.

2b8b16.evidence: All KB operations keyed by primary key with no organization_id predicate — verified by vitest PoC capturing Prisma where-clauses. Filed as vuln-0016.

a63ab3.surface: scopeMemberships.routes.ts + businessScopes raw-SQL endpoints + connector scope bindings
a63ab3.risk_area: IDOR / tenant isolation / scope membership escalation
a63ab3.evidence: Membership update/delete by primary key with no org predicate (verified by vitest PoC); plugins/mcp-servers raw SQL and getScopeConnectors lack organization predicate. Filed as vuln-0018.

0adf44.risk_area: Arbitrary-URL fetch from workflow action nodes (SSRF surface, member-authority)
0adf44.evidence: Covered by filed finding vuln-0009 (workflow api_call SSRF — member-authority arbitrary-URL fetch with attacker-controlled method/headers/body).

history.evidence: Member-role users can create workflows (requireModifyAccess) whose api_call action nodes fetch any URL with attacker-chosen method/headers/body from the backend host (workflow-orchestrator.ts:543-566, action-executor.ts:100-140), with variable substitution — classic SSRF/internal-network/metadata reach. Referred to the SSRF-focused team for dynamic validation to avoid duplicating their surface; no URL allowlist or private-range block exists in code.

d47219.evidence: requireAgentAccess and requireScopeAccess both verify request.user before checks; agentAccessService.checkAccess enforces org via findFirst({id, organization_id}); scopeAccessService.getAccessLevel filters business_scopes by organization_id. No fail-open catch, no query-param scoping. Skip-on-missing-id behavior exists but is only reachable when the route genuinely has no object id.

344472.risk_area: A2A API-key validation compares raw bearer token to sha256 hash column
344472.evidence: Filed as vuln-0008 (info/reliability defect); additionally the pass-the-hash property noted — a leaked key_hash becomes a valid credential until fixed.

history.evidence: validateApiKey does findFirst({key_hash: token}) comparing the raw bearer token to the sha256-hashed key stored by apiKeyService (sha256(key)). Because hash != key, no legitimately-issued key can ever authenticate — a functional/reliability defect, not an exploitable weakness: an attacker cannot authenticate either (they would need the hash value itself, which grants nothing since comparison is against key_hash, and supplying the stored hash would authenticate... actually supplying the sha256 hash AS the token WOULD match key_hash and authenticate).

Re-examined: validateApiKey (a2a.routes.ts:45-60) compares the raw bearer token to the sha256 `key_hash` column. Legitimately issued keys (sk_... whose sha256 is stored) can NEVER match, so A2A external auth is functionally broken; but anyone who obtains the stored hash value (DB read, backup, log leak) can use the hash itself as a valid credential (pass-the-hash). Not independently exploitable without DB read; flagged for the auth-focused team and as a reliability defect. Fix: compare sha256(token) to key_hash like apiKeyService.validateApiKey does.

1add7f.surface: backend src/routes/* update endpoints (agents, tasks, workflows, documents, organizations)
1add7f.evidence: All update bodies pass through Zod schemas with explicit field allowlists; none of createTaskSchema/updateTaskSchema/updateAgentSchema/updateDocumentSchema/updateMembershipSchema/connector schemas bind organization_id, user_id-owner, or role escalation fields (organization membership role changes are admin-gated and block owner promotion; agent schema has no organization_id/created_by at all).

38aaa6.risk_area: Double-execution race on scheduled workflow triggers
38aaa6.evidence: Filed as vuln-0028 (low, CWE-367): duplicate-trigger guard in processDueSchedules (schedule.service.ts:465-485) is non-atomic (findMany → non-atomic running check → execute); no lock/transaction/unique constraint. Overlap possible via async setInterval re-entry past 15s tick or the documented PROCESS_ROLE worker split (config/index.ts:108). Provided infra deploys a single instance/process, which constrains exploitability — severity low, confidence medium (static-only, no DB to run concurrent PoC).

history.evidence: The duplicate-trigger guard is non-atomic: the scheduler tick fetches due schedules, then updates next_run_at before executing; two concurrent ticks (multi-instance deployment or overlapping setInterval) both pass the fetch and both execute, and the findFirst(status:'scheduled') record-reuse can race (both update the same row to running, both run the workflow). Single-process default makes this latent; no DB-level lock or unique constraint prevents it. Business-logic/reliability issue, not confirmed dynamically.

156f04.risk_area: Quota bypass via concurrency (pre-flight check + 60s Redis cache)
156f04.evidence: Quota enforcement is explicitly best-effort by design (code comment at token-quota.service.ts: top): pre-flight check with 60s-cached usage and asynchronous consumption, so parallel requests can exceed quota. This is a documented design tradeoff (cost-control, not a security boundary), with plan defaults of 10M tokens/$100; not a security vulnerability — noted as an accepted business-logic limitation.

5dabb5.risk_area: A2A cross-agent invocation trust / authentication of remote agents
5dabb5.evidence: Room orchestration only ever constructs local:// endpoints from room members (chatRooms.routes.ts:295-303); no route or service passes a user-controlled https:// endpoint into a2aClient.sendTask, so the remote path is currently unreachable from user input. The remote-path auth weakness (buildRemoteHeaders sends Bearer <organizationId> placeholder, a2a-client.service.ts:159-165) is latent code with a TODO — no exploitable path found. Flagged as hardening debt, not a finding.

7e5661.surface: im.service.ts handleMessage + im-queue.service.ts + workspace file write path
7e5661.risk_area: IM-driven agent authority (prompt injection into credentialed agents)
7e5661.evidence: IM messages flow into chatService.processMessage with the binding creator's userId; attached files are written into the agent workspace (writeWorkspaceFileRaw has a containment check) and referenced in the prompt. The agent runtime then holds Bash/Write/WebFetch under bypassPermissions (vuln-0017) with a member JWT — no human-confirmation gate exists for chat/IM-triggered destructive actions. The authority-escalation root cause is reported in vuln-0017.

4245d8.risk_area: Workflow definition vs execution authorization; execution-record IDOR; humanApproval gating
4245d8.evidence: Create/update/import require requireModifyAccess, run requires authenticate+requireModifyAccess+enforceTokenQuota (execution.routes.ts:154); execution read/abort/logs/workspace routes all filter organization_id and GET /executions/:id additionally enforces per-user ownership for non-admins. humanApproval nodes genuinely pause execution via checkpoints. Remaining gap (checkpoint routes BOLA) is reported separately as vuln-0019.

18d28a.surface: workshop.service.ts, project-squad.service.ts, carry-forward.service.ts, rehearsal routes, support-workflow-executor, task.service.ts, agent-scope/scope-generator services
18d28a.evidence: Reviewed route/service wiring: all workshop/rehearsal/task/scope routes use authenticate (+requireModifyAccess for writes) and repository calls take organizationId; support-workflow-executor only dispatches to node-executor registry (faq/intent) without shell/network sinks; carry-forward copies scope config within org. No org-scoping gap or destructive sink found in these files; hooks and conversation-hooks are metrics-only (fire-and-forget, no side effects beyond status flags).

edae4a.evidence: No auth on WS route (no preHandler, no global auth hook) and no ownership check on subscribe; PoC-confirmed unauthenticated receipt of arbitrary execution events. Filed vuln-0020.

67e20e.surface: SSE endpoints (workflows.routes.ts, chat.routes.ts /sessions/:id/stream, chatRooms.routes.ts, widget.routes.ts, scope-generator.routes.ts, llm-proxy.routes.ts)
67e20e.evidence: All SSE routes carry preHandler [authenticate] or [apiKeyAuth/widgetAuth]; chat stream verifies session ownership via chatService.getSessionById(id, orgId); widget stream scoped by org; workflows execute-v2 resolves workflow by orgId. CORS `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` on SSE writeHead is a hygiene note only (no credentials in headers on that path).

3f0c4f.surface: super-agent/frontend message rendering (react-markdown usage, Chat.tsx, ChatRoom.tsx, TextContentBlock.tsx, hljs code preview)
3f0c4f.evidence: Markdown rendered via react-markdown without rehype-raw (no raw HTML pass-through); only dangerouslySetInnerHTML is hljs output on attacker-uncontrolled code content (hljs escapes input); HtmlPreview iframe uses sandbox="allow-scripts" (no allow-same-origin, opaque origin). IM/user message content flows into JSON APIs and React text nodes, not innerHTML. No DOMPurify needed given no raw HTML sink found.

11d9d1.surface: backend raw SQL usage (appData.routes.ts, scope-memory.repository.ts, knowledge-base.service.ts, rag/document-indexer.service.ts, middleware/auth.ts)
11d9d1.evidence: All $queryRawUnsafe/$executeRawUnsafe calls use positional $n placeholders for user-controlled values. appData.routes.ts interpolates JSONB keys but runs them through sanitizeKey() which strips to [a-zA-Z0-9_] — injection blocked. auth.ts email migration SQL is fully static with $1/$2 params.

e3224d.surface: credential vault + connectors + IM channel secrets (credential-vault.service.ts, connectors.routes.ts, im.routes.ts admin routes)
e3224d.evidence: Vault list/get strip encrypted fields; decryptCredential never exposed via API. IM binding responses mask bot_token_enc with '***'. Known hardcoded CONNECTOR_ENCRYPTION_KEY default already filed as vuln-0012 by another agent — not re-filed. Raw IM webhook secrets are stored plaintext in binding.config, but responses strip only bot_token_enc; config itself is returned in list responses (operator-configured signing secrets visible to org members) — noted as minor info disclosure, acceptable to scope owners.

88c7ef.evidence: gitleaks: 1 hit (demo SKILL.md MFA token marker, non-code demo content). trivy: 209 unique CVEs (2 critical, 77 high); top reported: fastify 5.6.2 validation/auth-bypass family (vuln-0021), axios 1.13.6 via IM SDKs (vuln-0022), js-yaml 4.1.1 in API-spec parser (vuln-0023). Default JWT_SECRET / connector key already covered by other agents' reports (vuln-0002, vuln-0012).

454c6a.evidence: /docs and /documentation are registered unconditionally including production (no isProduction guard) — an info-level exposure of full API surface (worth noting but low). Error handler: unexpected errors return generic 'Internal server error' without stack traces; stack traces only go to server-side pino logs (which redact authorization/cookie headers in production).

49221a.surface: im.routes.ts OAuth callback postMessage + widget SSE + request/audit logging
49221a.evidence: callbackHtml posts to window.opener with wildcard '*' target — only credentialId (not tokens) is posted; acceptable. requestLogger logs URL (query token leak already filed as vuln-0004 by auth agent). auditLog summarizes bodies but truncates long strings; no token-specific redaction beyond pino's header redaction.

44a8b1.risk_area: Plaintext secret exposure in binding config
44a8b1.evidence: List endpoint requires only `authenticate` (any member), spreads ...b with bot_token_enc masked to '***' but leaves `config` unmodified — exposes plaintext signing_secret/app_secret/secret_token/verification_token/encoding_aes_key. Org scoping IS correctly applied (repository where organization_id + business_scope_id), so same-org only. Filed as vuln-0027.
